system: You are a careful research assistant classifying public feedback. Output JSON only.
prompt:
Decide for each numbered item whether it is RELEVANT to a study of SIPs (systematic investment plans in mutual funds, incl. auto-invest / monthly mutual-fund investing) with three questions:
  (A) Why do people start a SIP, and what do they expect to happen?
  (B) What changes in their behaviour in the months after starting (checking returns, increasing, reducing, skipping, redeeming, switching, sticking with it)?
  (C) What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?

RELEVANT = the text describes the writer's own (or other investors') SIP experience, motives, expectations, behaviour or decisions that speak to A, B or C - including payment/mandate/app problems that make a SIP miss or stop.
NOT RELEVANT = generic praise or complaints about the app, stock trading only, SIPs merely named with nothing about motives/expectations/behaviour/decisions, spam or promotion, thanks to a video creator, or bare how-to questions with no personal situation.
The context line (video or forum topic title) is background only; judge the text.

Return a JSON array with one object per item: [{"i": <item number>, "relevant": true|false}]

[2] (source: valuepickr; context: Beginner investing questions about Direct vs Regular mutual funds, mistakes and learning resources)
Hey! Congratulations on starting your investing journey,
 To start with, try to keep a fix % of your income to invest via SIP.
 Let’s say if you earn 50,000 a month, then try to put 10-20% of it into SIP.
 Direct Growth/Regular won’t make much of a difference, Direct work fine for me. You get more units in regular (at a higher NAV price) vs in direct (Lesser units but lower entry NAV).
 Talking about mistakes, quite a few!! Most important is being patient and not having FOMO. Easier said than done.
 Have your thesis thoroughly ready, enter at a good point to keep buffer, be patient in waiting it to play out, once it does, don’t get out too early, monitor it closely and once the thesis start showing cracks, GET OUT.
 To start with:
Autobiography of a stock - Manoj Arora
 Little Book of Common Sense Investing - John Bogle
 Psychology of Money - Morgan Housel
 Websites like Investopedia, Screener, VP (ofcourse!), Varsity
 YT - SOIC, Exploring Minds.
 Hope this helps!

Good discussion, so adding my perspectives in general about SIP’s. Been doing SIP’s since 10 years, though increased the weightage of flow into SIP’s (vs direct equity) since 2020. Core idea behind SIP’ is its gives you the discipline and eliminates all the biases about market movements. To build a corpus and to continue your saving journey, SIP helps you immensely.
 Though I started with few Small caps, value funds and blue chip, later I realized, since maintaining a direct equity investment/demat, its better to go with index funds and ensuring general market returns on my SIP’s. So tilted a bit towards Nifty 50 and next 50, along Balance advantage fund to ensure stability of PF. The following are few points I found over the years, and I am still learning.
 Nifty 50 Index fund from ICICI was doing well for 4-5 yrs, but recently I found that its better to go with Factor funds with an index like Momentum/ Value, Low Volatility etc. So gradually shifted to Mom 30 and Low vol (out of 100/200).
 Few thematic fund like PHD, (Pharma, health, diagnostics) started prior to COVID, and still continuing. Pharma as a sector, not an easy segment to invest directly. Although I do have exposure to few pharma/hospital stocks, after 5-7 yrs, what I realized is we do miss a lot of good investment stories here.
